author: wooyeonkwon
body:
PR description:

This PR fixes a memory leak in RPCMonitorDigi::analyze() in DQM/RPCMonitorDigi/src/RPCMonitorDigi.cc.

Previously, each RPC rechit on the outer track of a selected muon was cloned using clone(), but the allocated object was never deleted.

Since only read-only access to the original rechit is required, the unnecessary cloning is replaced with a direct cast to a const RPCRecHit pointer.

This removes the unnecessary heap allocation while preserving the existing rechit processing logic. No changes to the DQM histogram contents are expected.

PR validation:

The fix was validated in CMSSW_20_1_0_pre5 (el9_amd64_gcc14) using a RelValZMM_14 Run-3 2026 no-pileup sample, with the Run3_2026 era and auto:phase1_2026_realistic global tag.

Only the rpcdigidqm module was run, using one thread and one stream, to isolate its memory usage.

Two independent memory validation tests were performed before and after applying the fix:

1. ModuleEventAllocMonitor

A total of 5,936 events were monitored after skipping the first 10 events.

| Metric | Before | After | | -- | -- | -- | | Allocations never freed | 26,652 | 8 | | Events with memory growth | 4,688 | 265 | | Module memory growth (--grew) | 2,780,104 B | 222,952 B | | Average net memory growth per event | 468.5 B | 37.6 B |

The number of allocations never freed was reduced by 99.97%, and the RSS growth rate was reduced by approximately 95%.

Both tests demonstrate that the sustained memory growth associated with the unnecessary RPC rechit cloning is removed.

The modified package was successfully rebuilt using scram b. A direct comparison of the DQM histogram contents was not performed; however, identical output is expected because the same RPC rechit values are copied into rechitMuon. RSS as a function of the number of processed events before and after the fix. Only the `rpcdigidqm` module was run using the RelValZMM_14 Run-3 2026 no-pileup sample, repeated 50 times. The fitted RSS growth rate after the first 20,000 events decreases from 431 B/event to 22 B/event.

title: Fix potential memory leak in RPCMonitorDigi
